reference.source: U.S. Naval Air Station Patuxent River, 'Performance Test Each 1000th Airplane' (TED No. PTR-2125), 7 Sep 1944, F6F-5 BuNo 58310, Overload Fighter loading, military-power trial data as tabulated at wwiiaircraftperformance.org/f6f/f6f.html (summary table re-read 2026-09-12). That table states 'Gross weight -lbs 12,420' for this airplane, which is testMassKg = 5633.62 kg -- so the trial weight is stated and no substitution of a published normal-loaded weight was needed. topSpeedMps = 391.0 mph at an airplane critical altitude of 23,100 ft; climbRateMps = 2,660 ft/min at sea level. stallSpeedMps = 98.0 mph, the table's CLEAN, POWER-OFF stall: the flight model has no flaps or landing gear, so the clean figure is the like-for-like one. The same table's landing-condition power-off stall is 84.5 mph (37.77 m/s), which an earlier revision of this file cited by mistake -- it is unreachable for a model with no high-lift devices. Weights and dimensions cross-checked against the Grumman F6F Hellcat Wikipedia infobox (334 sq ft / 31.0 sq m wing, 42 ft 10 in / 13.06 m span, 9,238 lb / 4,190 kg empty). rollRateDegPerSec is NOT corroborated by this source and remains an unsourced estimate. takeoffDistanceM is the SAME table's 'Take-off distance, no wind' row: 755 ft = 230.124 m, FULL FLAPS, take-off speed 86.5 mph, 2700 RPM -- the table's other take-off figure, 335 ft in a 25-knot wind, is not used because the model carries no wind (Ruling R29). This is NOT a like-for-like figure: the model has no flaps (which pushes a simulated roll shorter than a full-flaps trial roll -- no flap drag to slow the acceleration) and no ground effect (which pushes it longer -- ground effect cuts induced drag and adds lift near the surface, both of which shorten a real roll, so a model missing it does not get that shortening). Plan 11a (2026-09-16) added rolling friction, which is now modelled and pushes the roll longer, moving the model from a -6.73% to a -0.605% under-estimate against the same trial figure. The take-off card grades this at a tolerance TIGHTENED, not widened, to 2% -- a characterisation lock on engine.staticThrustN, gear.rollingResistanceCoeff and reference.testMassKg rather than evidence of full flight-model fidelity, since flaps and ground effect still don't apply -- see tools/testcards/measure.ts and f6f.test.ts for the tolerance and the evidence it is built from. gear.travelSeconds and gear.dragAreaM2 are NOT corroborated by this source, or by NACA WR L-716 either: neither document times the gear cycle or gives a drag increment for it. Like rollRateDegPerSec above, both remain unsourced estimates -- 7 seconds is a round figure in line with the hydraulically-actuated retractable gear typical of WWII single-engine fighters of this class, and 0.3 sq m of drag area is a round, deliberately modest guess at the equivalent flat-plate area of two extended main legs, wheels and doors, well under the airplane's own zero-lift drag area of wingAreaM2 * cd0 = 0.65 sq m. Both are placeholders for Mark to retune once the airplane can actually be flown with the gear down. gear.rollingResistanceCoeff (0.02) and gear.brakingResistanceCoeff (0.4) are likewise NOT corroborated by this source or by NACA WR L-716 -- neither document measures ground rolling friction -- and are round, generic figures for a pneumatic tire on a hard runway (unbraked rolling resistance in the low hundredths; brakes-locked friction in the range commonly cited for aircraft tires), not F6F-specific data. gear.tailUpSpeedMps (15) and gear.tailwheelYawRateDegPerSec (20) are the same kind of unsourced estimate: no trial in this source times when the tail comes unstuck or how fast the tailwheel can swing the nose, so both are round, plausible placeholders -- tailUpSpeedMps well below the 38.67 m/s (86.5 mph) full-flap take-off speed the same table reports, and tailwheelYawRateDegPerSec picked independently of rates.maxYawRateDegPerSec's 15 deg/s of airborne rudder authority -- ground steering and airborne rudder are different mechanisms, so no relationship between the two numbers should be read into either value. All four are placeholders for Mark to retune once the airplane can actually be taxied. windmillCd0 = 0.0422 is an ENGINEERING ESTIMATE, not a trial figure, and is labeled as one here for the same reason rollRateDegPerSec is: no wind-tunnel or flight-test figure for a windmilling R-2800 disc on this airframe was located. It is 2.00x the clean cd0 of 0.0211 -- a windmilling constant-speed propeller roughly doubles clean parasitic drag -- taken as the MIDDLE of the published 1x-3x range for a stopped or windmilling propeller, which spans that much depending on blade pitch. Measured on this airplane 2026-09-16, level at 50 ft with altitude pinned so drag is the only loss, 250 mph bleeding to 100 mph: 79.3 s / 6.01 km with no propeller drag at all (the state Mark flew and reported as unrealistic), 50.5 s at 1x, 37.5 s / 2.70 km at this value, 30.0 s at 3x. Expect to tune it once someone flies a dead-stick approach. gear.heightM = 2.42 is an ESTIMATE, not a trial figure -- neither this table nor NACA WR L-716 gives a static ground clearance or thrust-line height for the type. It is the drawn model's own stance: since sortie forms amendment A4 (2026-09-27) the Hellcat is drawn with its R3 model (content/aircraft/f6f-hellcat.glb), whose main wheels sit 2.424 m below its origin, and tests/tools/models/aircraftRigs.test.ts holds this figure to that mesh within 0.05 m (the rule R3's ruling P1 set for every drawn aircraft). The earlier 2.2 m (2026-09-16) was derived from the real F6F-5's 13 ft 1 in (3.99 m) propeller with about 9 in (0.23 m) of tip clearance, and fitted the Wildcat model the Hellcat was drawn with until A4. view.eyePointM = [-0.75, 0.95, 0] is MEASURED from the drawn model (2026-09-28): under the apex of its canopy node kabina-FACES (x -0.72, y 1.27), 0.3 m below it. The Wildcat-era [1.2, 0.9, 0] it replaces sat 2 m forward, over the engine cowling. tests/tools/models/eyePoints.test.ts holds it inside that canopy. Gear layout (added 2026-09-28): gear.mainX, thirdX and thirdHeightM are measured from the drawn model with drawnPoints (the first aft point to touch when the model is pitched about the mains); layout and the tail-wheel steering, brake, tail-lift, prop-wash and torque fields are ESTIMATE.

combat.source: Six .50-cal guns: National Naval Aviation Museum https://www.history.navy.mil/content/history/museums/nnam/explore/collections/aircraft/f/f6f-5-hellcat.html . 800 rpm is a choice within the 750-850 rpm range and 883.92 m/s converts 2900 ft/s in the US Navy Aircrewman's Gunnery Manual https://www.ibiblio.org/hyperwar/USN/ref/AirGunnery/GUNS.html . 400 rounds/gun: Patriots Point Naval & Maritime Museum https://patriotspoint.org/things-to-do/aircraft/f6f-hellcat . Verified 2026-09-19. Convergence, dispersion, lifetime, drag, HP, per-hit damage, leak/decay rates, mounts and hit zones are gameplay ESTIMATES. Hitboxes approximate the existing procedural mesh, not a sourced installation drawing. No penetration model.

stores.source: Six HVARs, three under each wing; single bomb racks under each wing inboard of the undercarriage bays; 1,000 lb class per rack: English Wikipedia, 'Grumman F6F Hellcat', read 2026-09-20. HVAR: 134 lb (61 kg) all-up, 45.5 lb (20.6 kg) warhead, 1,375 ft/s (419 m/s) plus the speed of the launching aircraft: English Wikipedia, 'High Velocity Aircraft Rocket', read 2026-09-20; designation-systems.net 'Air-Launched 5-Inch Rockets' gives 64 kg / 20 kg / 5 km range. Burn time 1.0 s is an ESTIMATE: neither source states it. AN-M65 1,000 lb GP: 530 lb (240.9 kg) Amatol filler, 53% of total weight, so 1,000 lb (453.6 kg) all-up: Australian War Memorial C285409 and bulletpicker.com 'Bomb, 1000 lb GP, AN-M44, AN-M65, AN-M65A1', read 2026-09-20. dragAreaM2, dragPerM, damage, roundDamage, blastRadiusM, armS, lifetimeS are ESTIMATES or gameplay choices, in the same standing as combat's dispersion and HP figures. dragPerM for the bomb was chosen against an estimate of "about 1,200 m downrange and roughly 200 m/s" for a release at 120 m/s from 1,500 m; measured 2026-09-22 by tests/sim/strike.test.ts, which is where Plan 6b said the actual figure would be recorded, it is 17.67 s of fall, 2,066 m downrange and 202.9 m/s at the water. The speed estimate held; the range estimate did not, and this sentence carries the measurement instead of the guess. Rack and rail OFFSETS are measured on the wing of the model this spec draws: since sortie forms amendment A4 (2026-09-27) that is the Hellcat's own R3 model, built level (datum pitch 0) in the sim frame. `npm run models:mounts` slices that wing at each rack's and rail's lateral station (unchanged since before O1) and hangs the store at 40% (bomb) or 50% (rocket) of the chord, 2 cm clear of the lower skin; the chord fractions and the clearance are ESTIMATES. From 2026-09-26 (plan O1) until A4 the offsets were measured on the drawn Wildcat instead, about 1.3 m above the origin. Re-measured 2026-09-27 on the Hellcat's own wing: 17.67 s of fall (1060 ticks), 2,065.8 m downrange and 202.9 m/s (tests/sim/strike.test.ts); the O1 offsets gave 1061 / 2,069.6 / 203.0.
